data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's Lexical Divergence Metric is a cross-run analog of a paper-turing test: it measures whether the check looks different, not whether it is independent. Its own countercondition concedes the flaw — a checker can use synonyms to mask restatement of the same logical path. But the proposed remedy (counting the intersection of cited source IDs) does not fix this: a checker can cite disjoint source IDs yet still mechanically re-walk the author's derivation without re-deriving anything, or cite the same canonical sources in a different surface form. Conversely, genuine independent verification of a narrow claim may necessarily cite the same single artifact (the countercondition admits domains with only one possible supporting evidence). So the metric both under-detects restatement and over-penalizes genuine verification. The problem asks what evidence distinguishes genuine independent verification from restatement, and where a claim can be tested by counting or execution, say exactly what to count or execute; 'count citation-ID overlap' is neither sufficient (disjoint IDs ≠ independence) nor necessary (same IDs ≠ restatement).
